capabilities.title: Web Applications
capabilities.description: Responsive, scalable applications that give customers and internal teams a faster way to get work done.
capabilities.headline: Give people a better way to get work done.
capabilities.summary: Web applications are interactive websites that help people get tasks done online. Customers or employees can sign in, manage information, submit requests, and complete work from a browser.
capabilities.example: A company wants customers to create accounts, submit service requests, track their progress, and manage their details online, without phone calls or email chains.
builds: Responsive web applications for any screen size

steps.label: Understand
steps.text: Learn how the work happens today and where it gets stuck.

steps.label: Plan
steps.text: Agree on the screens, features, and who uses what.

steps.label: Build
steps.text: Design and develop the application in working stages.

steps.label: Release
steps.text: Test with real tasks and prepare it for launch.

capabilities.outcome: Customers and teams get a more convenient way to complete tasks, without relying on disconnected tools or manual processes.

capabilities.title: SaaS Products
capabilities.description: Multi-user platforms, dashboards, subscriptions and workflows designed to support real product operations.
capabilities.headline: One online product, serving many customers.
capabilities.summary: SaaS ("software as a service") is software people use online, often through a subscription. Many customers use the same platform, while each one’s account and information stay properly separated.
capabilities.example: A business wants to offer an online appointment management platform that many different companies can sign up for and use.
builds: User accounts, with different access for different roles
Dashboards and the core product workflows
Subscription and billing connections, when required

steps.label: Understand
steps.text: Define who the customers are and what they need to do.

steps.label: Plan
steps.text: Decide on account types, access rules, and billing needs.

steps.label: Build
steps.text: Develop the platform, dashboards, and admin tools.

steps.label: Release
steps.text: Test with realistic accounts and prepare for launch.

capabilities.outcome: An online product that can serve many customers and grow as the business develops.
capabilities.note: Subscriptions, payment integrations, and how customer data is separated (often called "multi-tenant" setup) depend on your product’s requirements. We agree on these with you before building.

capabilities.title: Business Software
capabilities.description: ERP, CRM, PMS, internal tools and automation that match how the business actually runs.
capabilities.headline: Run daily operations from one place.
capabilities.summary: Business software helps a company organize its daily operations in one place. It brings together information, tasks, staff, customers, and processes that would otherwise live in separate tools.
capabilities.example: A growing company keeps customers in spreadsheets, staff tasks in chat messages, and project progress in separate documents. A custom system can bring all of that together.
builds: ERP-style workflows for operations, stock, or finance

steps.label: Understand
steps.text: Map how your team works today, step by step.

steps.label: Plan
steps.text: Choose what to bring together first and what can wait.

steps.label: Build
steps.text: Develop the system around your real workflow.

steps.label: Release
steps.text: Test with the people who will use it every day.

capabilities.outcome: Everyday operations become easier to manage, with less unnecessary manual work.
capabilities.note: CRM means customer relationship management; ERP means software that connects core operations like stock, orders, and finance. The exact features depend on your workflow and the agreed scope.

capabilities.title: Backend & APIs
capabilities.description: Secure APIs, integrations, databases and business logic that keep products reliable as usage grows.
capabilities.headline: The reliable engine behind your product.
capabilities.summary: The backend is the part of an application that works behind the scenes. It processes information, applies business rules, stores data, and connects different systems. An API is the agreed way two systems ask each other for information.
capabilities.example: When a customer places an order, the backend records it, calculates the totals, updates its status, and gives both the customer and your staff the information they need.
builds: APIs that let your apps and other systems talk to each other
Sign-in and access control, so people only see what they should
Background tasks that run without slowing anyone down

steps.label: Understand
steps.text: Learn what information moves where, and the rules it follows.

steps.label: Plan
steps.text: Design the data structure and how systems will connect.

steps.label: Build
steps.text: Develop the APIs, rules, and integrations.

steps.label: Release
steps.text: Test reliability, permissions, and error handling.

capabilities.outcome: Applications exchange information reliably and handle business operations consistently.

capabilities.title: Frontend Engineering
capabilities.description: Modern interfaces with clear flows, polished interactions, accessibility and strong performance.
capabilities.headline: Interfaces people understand at a glance.
capabilities.summary: Frontend engineering is building the parts of a website or app that people see and use. It turns designs into working screens that are easy to use on desktop, tablet, and mobile.
capabilities.example: A company has a design for a new website and needs it turned into a responsive experience with working navigation, forms, dashboards, and interactive elements.
builds: Interactive dashboards and step-by-step user journeys

steps.label: Understand
steps.text: Review the design and what each screen must do.

steps.label: Plan
steps.text: Break the design into reusable pieces and user flows.

steps.label: Build
steps.text: Develop the screens and connect them to real data.

steps.label: Release
steps.text: Test on different devices, browsers, and with a keyboard.

capabilities.outcome: People understand the product quickly, move through it confidently, and finish their tasks with less friction.

capabilities.title: System Modernization
capabilities.description: Improve existing platforms by reducing friction, strengthening architecture and clarifying the user experience.
capabilities.headline: Improve what you have, without starting over.
capabilities.summary: System modernization means improving an existing website or application rather than automatically rebuilding it from scratch. The goal is to remove limitations, improve usability, and make it easier to maintain and extend.
capabilities.example: A business relies on an older application that is hard to use, slow to update, and expensive to maintain. It can be assessed and improved in stages, while it keeps running.
builds: Cleaning up code that is hard to maintain
Connecting existing systems with newer tools

steps.label: Assess
steps.text: Review the current system, its limits, and its risks.

steps.label: Plan
steps.text: Agree which improvements matter most, and in what order.

steps.label: Improve
steps.text: Make changes in stages, keeping the system usable.

steps.label: Release
steps.text: Test each stage carefully before it goes live.

capabilities.outcome: Existing software lasts longer, works with less friction, and has a clearer path for future improvements.
capabilities.note: Every system is different. We can only recommend what to improve, keep, or replace after a detailed technical assessment.

services.title: Product Development
services.headline: Turn your idea into a working product.
services.summary: We turn your idea into a working digital product. From planning the features to building and launching it, we help bring your idea to life.
services.example: You have an idea for an app that helps people book appointments with local professionals. We can help turn that idea into a product people can actually use.

steps.label: Understand
steps.text: Understand your idea and the problem it solves.

steps.label: Plan
steps.text: Plan the important features and how people will use them.

steps.label: Build
steps.text: Design and build the product.

steps.label: Launch
steps.text: Test it and prepare it for launch.

services.audience: Entrepreneurs, startups, and businesses creating a new digital product.

services.title: Business Software
services.headline: Run your everyday work from one organized place.
services.summary: We build software that helps your business manage everyday work more easily. Instead of juggling things by hand, your team keeps information and tasks in one organized place.
services.example: A service business tracks customers, appointments, invoices, and staff schedules in separate spreadsheets. We can build one system that brings all of these together.

steps.label: Observe
steps.text: Understand how your business works day to day.

steps.label: Identify
steps.text: Find the repetitive tasks and common problems.

steps.label: Build
steps.text: Build software around the way your team works.

steps.label: Refine
steps.text: Test it with the people who will use it.

services.audience: Small businesses, growing companies, and teams that need software suited to the way they actually work.

services.title: SaaS Platforms
services.headline: Offer your software online to many customers.
services.summary: SaaS means "software as a service": software people use through a web browser instead of installing it. Customers can sign up, use its features, and manage their own accounts.
services.example: A company wants to offer an online booking service that many different businesses can subscribe to and use from their browsers.

steps.label: Plan
steps.text: Plan the service and the different kinds of users.

steps.label: Build
steps.text: Build accounts, features, and the tools to manage them.

steps.label: Monetize
steps.text: Add subscriptions or payments, if your product needs them.

steps.label: Launch
steps.text: Test the platform and prepare it for launch.

deliverables: User accounts and access levels, where needed
A dashboard to manage the platform
Subscription or payment features, if your product needs them
services.audience: Startups and businesses that want to offer an online software service to many customers.

services.title: API & Backend Systems
services.headline: The engine that works behind the scenes.
services.summary: The backend is the part of software you don’t see. It stores and processes information, applies your business rules, and lets different apps talk to each other safely. An API is the agreed way those apps exchange information.
services.example: When a customer places an order on a shopping website, the backend saves the order, updates its status, and shows the right details in the customer’s account.

steps.label: Map
steps.text: Understand what information your application needs.

steps.label: Organize
steps.text: Organize the data and the rules it must follow.

steps.label: Connect
steps.text: Build the systems that handle requests and connect apps.

steps.label: Verify
steps.text: Test reliability, permissions, and how data is handled.

deliverables: Systems that process your application’s data
A database and your business rules, built in
Sensible access controls and error handling
services.audience: Businesses building applications, connecting services, or managing information across several systems.

services.title: Frontend Engineering
services.headline: The part of your website people see and use.
services.summary: Frontend engineering is building the screens people see and click on. We turn designs into pages that respond, feel smooth, and work on phones, tablets, and computers.
services.example: A business has a website design but needs it turned into a working site with navigation, forms, animations, and layouts that fit mobile screens.

steps.label: Review
steps.text: Review the design and what the site needs to do.

steps.label: Build
steps.text: Build the page layouts and reusable pieces.

steps.label: Connect
steps.text: Make buttons, forms, and data work as they should.

steps.label: Test
steps.text: Test the experience on desktop, tablet, and mobile.

deliverables: Website screens that fit every device
services.audience: Businesses, designers, startups, and development teams that need polished, working web interfaces.

services.title: Automation
services.headline: Let software handle the repetitive tasks.
services.summary: Automation lets software take care of routine tasks for you. When something specific happens, the system carries out the next steps on its own, so your team spends less time on busywork.
services.example: When someone fills in a contact form, a system could save the enquiry, notify your sales team, and send the customer a confirmation email.

steps.label: Spot
steps.text: Find the repetitive tasks and the rules they follow.

steps.label: Define
steps.text: Decide what should start each action.

steps.label: Connect
steps.text: Connect the tools you use, or build the workflow.

steps.label: Test
steps.text: Test the workflow and plan for when things go wrong.

deliverables: Connections between tools you use, where they support it
A clearer view of what each workflow is doing
services.audience: Businesses and teams that spend time on repetitive data entry, notifications, reports, or routine admin work.
